channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: United Airlines bars unauthorized AI agents from booking travel
item.description: United Airlines barred unauthorized third-party AI agents from booking, purchasing, or servicing travel through its digital platforms. The airline cited data privacy risks, account security concerns, and potential violations of FAA and DOT regulations. The policy highlights a growing pushback from major consumer businesses against autonomous AI agents performing transactions on behalf of users.

item.title: Google launches Gemini Decisions API for fast multimodal yes/no and choice scoring
item.description: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API, powered by the Gemini Decision 1 model, allowing up to 1,000 bounded-choice questions per request across text, images, audio, video and PDFs. The service costs $0.10 per million input tokens and returns probabilities in 150‑250 ms. It gives developers a low‑cost, low‑latency way to automate policy checks, routing and grading without using expensive generative models.

item.title: Edelbyte emerges from stealth with $70M for AI agent data platform
item.description: Edelbyte emerged from stealth with $70 million in funding led by Sequoia and Quiet Capital to build a data analytics platform optimized for AI agents. The startup offers a unified platform combining search, analytics, vector, graph, and geospatial capabilities. The funding highlights investor backing for data infrastructure built specifically to handle the query volumes and access patterns generated by AI agents.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video details multi-chip strategy and compute multipliers
item.description: Simon Willison published a transcript of Anthropic's IPO roadshow video, which includes a section with co-founder Tom Brown on how Anthropic trains and serves Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and AMD GPUs. The video also describes "compute multipliers" and says an internal tool called Mythos ported Claude to AMD GPUs in three days. The roadshow video gives a rare look at how Anthropic structures its compute across four chip families and how it frames efficiency gains as a competitive moat ahead of its Nasdaq debut.

item.title: Google DeepMind announces AlphaGenome 2 DNA sequence model
item.description: Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaGenome 2, a DNA sequence model that predicts how genetic variants affect specific human cell types and states. Trained on over 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues, the model identifies nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression as its predecessor. AlphaGenome 2 bridges single-cell biology and human genetics by moving from broad tissue averages to individual cell types, helping researchers uncover cellular drivers of disease.

item.title: Google DeepMind uses AI to formally verify key parts of Signal encryption
item.description: DeepMind researchers employed the AlphaProof Code framework and Gemini Carbon agents to mathematically prove several cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol in a four‑week proof‑of‑concept. The analysis found no new vulnerabilities and correctly flagged known, fixed bugs in older versions. It shows AI can speed up formal verification, offering stronger assurance for the encryption that protects billions of messages.

item.title: Anthropic IPO draws multiple times the orders for available shares
item.description: Anthropic's initial public offering has drawn multiple times the orders for available shares. The Claude maker is reportedly planning a livestreamed marketing event on Friday featuring CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon. The high demand for Anthropic's shares highlights strong investor interest as the first major standalone frontier AI lab prepares to enter public trading.

item.title: Torus raises $500M to build modular container-sized AI data centers
item.description: Salt Lake City-based energy storage startup Torus raised a $500 million Series C round led by Magnetar to launch its new Foundry product, which packs power, storage, cooling, networking, and AI computing into shipping container-sized units. The modular units range in size from one to 20 megawatts and are designed to run AI inference tasks at existing business and factory sites. This $500 million raise highlights how energy storage companies are capitalizing on power grid constraints by packaging AI computing into modular units that utilize existing electrical capacity at commercial sites.

item.title: SoftBank writes off $3.7B from unused gas turbines for AI data centres
item.description: SoftBank reserved enough gas turbines to generate the power of six Hoover Dams (13GW+) for AI data centres and has written off $3.7 billion in losses from equipment it no longer needs. The company also recorded a separate ~$1.3 billion loss tied to warrants granted to OpenAI. It shows the scale of financial risk in securing power for AI data centres, where advance payments for equipment can turn into billions in losses when plans change.

item.title: AvenuesAI reports Q2 net profit of Rs 72 cr and 47% revenue surge
item.description: Digital payments company AvenuesAI reported a 6% increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 71.7 crore for the September quarter of FY27. Revenue from operations rose 47% year-on-year to Rs 2,879.2 crore. The results highlight the growth and margin pressures in the digital payments and fintech sector as companies scale transaction volumes amid increasing competition.

item.title: NHA selects EkaCare for AI Voice Scribe in public health facilities
item.description: The National Health Authority selected health AI startup EkaCare as a technology partner for its ambient AI Voice Scribe solution in public health facilities. The tool converts doctor-patient conversations into structured clinical notes in Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources format across more than 15 Indian languages. This partnership integrates ambient AI voice technology into public health facilities under India's Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission to reduce medical documentation burdens.

item.title: Madras High Court rules AI-generated books violate library rules, orders FIR
item.description: The Madras High Court ruled that AI-generated and plagiarised books fall under 'doubtful taste' and cannot be procured by public libraries. The court ordered the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption to immediately register an FIR regarding alleged fraudulent book purchases in Tamil Nadu. This ruling establishes a legal precedent in India restricting the public procurement of AI-generated and plagiarised content under library rules.

item.title: Nvidia spy scandal exposes Singapore chip networks evading US export controls
item.description: The Nvidia spy scandal has exposed networks operating in Singapore that help Chinese tech companies access advanced U.S. AI chips and circumvent export controls. Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The scandal brings heightened government scrutiny to the distribution networks and intermediary companies used to move advanced AI hardware across international borders.

item.title: US and China should stay clear-eyed on AI cooperation and competition, says Bessent
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the US and China must navigate AI cooperation to mitigate risks while competing for supremacy. The two nations plan to advance a bilateral dialogue on superintelligence and establish an AI alert system. It highlights how the world's leading economies are formalizing risk management and direct communication channels for advanced artificial intelligence while maintaining competitive postures.

item.title: Nothing teases screenless AI hardware device launching in December
item.description: Nothing CEO Carl Pei has teased the company's first AI-native hardware device ahead of a planned launch in December 2026. A teaser video shows a compact metallic gadget featuring two red and green LED lights, a physical button, and no display. The gadget highlights an emerging push toward screenless AI hardware focused on capturing real-world conversational context rather than relying on chat interfaces.

item.title: PLA-linked Chinese university obtained Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist
item.description: Procurement records show that China's Northwestern Polytechnical University bought Nvidia H200 chips and rented computing capacity last month despite being on a US export blacklist. The purchases highlight gaps in Washington's export controls aimed at restricting China's access to advanced technology. The findings underscore challenges in enforcing export curbs against blacklisted entities and have intensified Washington scrutiny on Nvidia and its leadership regarding sales to China.

item.title: PuppyGraph raises $10m Series A to help AI agents query enterprise tables
item.description: PuppyGraph has raised a $10 million Series A round led by Particle Future to support engineering and enterprise expansion. The funding follows the general availability of PuppyGraph 1.0, which allows AI agents to query up to 3,000 enterprise tables as a unified graph. The funding and version 1.0 release highlight growing infrastructure investments to help AI agents navigate complex enterprise data across multiple systems without data duplication.

item.title: Jensen Huang affair raises chances of US chip export limits in NDAA
item.description: Sources report that Jensen Huang's affair has significantly raised the chances of Congress enacting chip export limits this year. The measure is being considered via the National Defense Authorization Act. The espionage scandal surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is posing an escalating threat to the chipmaker's export operations and legislative outcomes in Washington.

item.title: Bombay High Court quashes customs order citing AI-hallucinated judgments
item.description: The Bombay High Court quashed a customs department order after the petitioner pointed out that the decision cited two non-existent Supreme Court judgments. The customs department agreed to scrap the order, and the court directed the commissioner to issue a fresh decision. This case demonstrates the legal risks and judicial consequences of relying on unverified AI-generated content in administrative and judicial decisions.

item.title: Ethan Mollick tests Fable 5.2 and Gemini Carbon on the Fermi Paradox
item.description: Ethan Mollick asked Fable 5.2 and Gemini Carbon to solve the Fermi Paradox. The models did not solve the paradox, but produced interesting outputs. It illustrates how educators and researchers are testing different AI models on complex, open-ended scientific questions.

item.title: eBay blocks AI shopping agents; Amazon, Target, Walmart take different stances
item.description: eBay has blocked AI shopping agents, including Meta's Muse, from browsing its listings, joining Amazon in restricting such bots while Target permits approved providers and Walmart partners with AI companies. BrightEdge estimates agent-driven purchases are up 43% monthly, yet only about 3% of e-commerce firms let agents complete transactions. It shows the practical limits of agentic AI shopping: even as agents grow, major retailers are deciding who gets access, which shapes how useful these tools can be for consumers.

item.title: Anthropic opens Australian retail IPO ahead of Nasdaq listing
item.description: Anthropic opened its Australian retail initial public offering, giving individual investors less than a week to buy Class A shares. The company is offering 825 million shares globally at $70 to $78 each ahead of its Nasdaq listing. The offering provides retail investors access to one of the largest technology share deals, valuing the AI company at up to $1.404 trillion.

item.title: AMD launches Zen 6 EPYC Venice processors with up to 256 cores
item.description: AMD has announced the availability of its EPYC 9006 \"Venice\" series processors featuring up to 256 Zen 6c cores per socket. The new enterprise processors utilize a 2nm manufacturing process and support up to 16 channels of DDR5-8000 or MRDIMM-12800 memory. The release of Zen 6 EPYC processors marks AMD's transition to a 2nm process node and introduces higher core counts for enterprise servers and HPC workloads.

item.title: OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved to -109% in Q3
item.description: Leaked documents show OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% in Q2 to -109% in Q3. During the same period, the company's revenue grew by roughly 50% to reach $10 billion. The leaked figures provide a rare look at OpenAI's financial performance, showing narrowing adjusted operating losses alongside rapid revenue growth driven by enterprise customers.

item.title: Amazon announces Ring AI security drone and roving business robot
item.description: Amazon's Ring launched a new robotics division debuting the Ring Drone Cam indoor flying camera for $249.99 and the Ring Rover Cam business robot for $999.99. Both autonomous devices use an AI Pilot system to map floor plans, navigate obstacles, and respond to security triggers. Amazon is expanding its consumer and enterprise security hardware ecosystem from stationary cameras into autonomous mobile robots.

item.title: CoreWeave reports Q3 revenue up 168% YoY to $3.66B and $132.5B backlog
item.description: CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, beating analyst estimates of $3.55 billion and marking a 168% year-over-year increase. The company also posted a net loss of $709 million and grew its revenue backlog to $132.5 billion. The financial results provide insight into neocloud infrastructure spending, debt financing, and customer demand amid questions about capital requirements for artificial intelligence buildouts.

item.title: Apple's Claris unit testing Harbor app to run local AI models on Macs
item.description: Apple's Claris subsidiary is testing an app called Harbor that turns Apple silicon Macs into a private AI inference server, with support for clustering multiple Macs over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory. The app is in private preview and not yet publicly available. Apple's entry into local AI tooling with a no-command-line interface could lower the barrier for developers and businesses to run open-weight models on their own hardware without cloud dependency.

item.title: OpenAI reports $10 billion in Q3 revenue as enterprise demand grows
item.description: OpenAI told investors its revenue jumped 50% to around $10 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up from 17% growth in the second quarter. More than half of the revenue came from enterprise clients, driven by demand for APIs and newer models like GPT-5.6 and Astra. The figures show rapid financial growth for leading AI labs, with enterprise clients and major partners like Microsoft capturing significant market activity.

item.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks confidential data from thousands of user apps
item.description: Security researchers found that thousands of apps created using SpaceXSI's Grok Build coding agent exposed confidential business, employee, and personal data because they could be accessed without sign-in. Out of 37,571 tested apps, 35,578 opened without authentication, including 24 internal apps belonging to SpaceXSI. The incident demonstrates how easy it is for AI coding tools to unintentionally publish sensitive corporate databases and internal documents to the public internet when proper access controls are missing by default.

item.title: Nvidia plans $10B investment in Anthropic alongside its IPO
item.description: Nvidia plans to invest $10 billion in Anthropic alongside its initial public offering. The commitment is part of a larger funding effort that includes public share sales and private deals with multiple technology giants. The investment highlights the deepening financial ties between major artificial intelligence labs and hardware providers as they secure massive capital deployments.
